title: §22-001: Database Systems Overview & Driver Connection Pooling
description: Multiple-choice practice questions and deep runtime verification for §22-001 (Database Systems Overview & Driver Connection Pooling).

cards.concept: Database Systems Overview & Driver Connection Pooling: Database Connection Pool Management
cards.question: Why must database client acquisitions from a connection pool always be wrapped in a `try...finally` block?

options.text: To encrypt the SQL connection during queries.
To guarantee that `client.release()` is executed even if the query throws an exception, preventing connection pool starvation.
To automatically commit transactions upon return.
To clear memory heap buffers.

cards.explanation: If a database client is acquired and an exception occurs before release() is called, the connection leaks. Repeated leaks deplete available connections, hanging the application.
cards.pitfall: Failing to release pooled connections in error handling paths exhausts pool capacity, causing subsequent requests to time out.

cards.concept: Database Systems Overview & Driver Connection Pooling: Database Statement Timeouts
cards.question: Why should production Node.js services configure explicit `statement_timeout` on relational database connections?

options.text: To speed up query compilation.
To automatically terminate runaway queries (e.g. unindexed full table scans or lock deadlocks) before they exhaust database CPU and connection pool slots.
To disable query caching.
To force transactions to run in read-only mode.

cards.explanation: Unbounded queries that encounter lock contention or unindexed tables can hold database connections indefinitely. Statement timeouts abort queries exceeding safe thresholds (e.g. 5000ms).
cards.pitfall: Leaving statement_timeout at 0 (unlimited) allows a single accidental slow query to back up connection pools and cause cascaded system failure.
